claims.claim: Eaton is exposed to a physical power-infrastructure bottleneck: data-center and broader electrification load growth require distribution, protection and related electrical equipment before incremental compute or industrial load can operate.
The company-specific causal capture depends on sustained orders/backlog, manufacturing capacity, mix and integration execution; load growth alone does not guarantee Eaton margins or share.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Electrical infrastructure is a prerequisite layer for data-center and electrification expansion, with strong order/backlog evidence.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Demand is supported by multiple load-growth pathways beyond a single AI architecture, including broader electrification.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Electrical distribution/protection needs persist, but product/vendor substitution and project timing can shift company capture.

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks include manufacturing capacity, project timing and integration/mix execution as demand scales.

causalEdges.mechanism: new loads require safe, reliable electrical infrastructure
causalEdges.falsifier: electrical orders/backlog contract despite sustained load growth

causalEdges.mechanism: Eaton captures projects through its electrical portfolio and installed-channel position
causalEdges.falsifier: industry demand stays strong while Eaton orders/share weaken

causalEdges.mechanism: volume and operating leverage can convert demand into cash
causalEdges.falsifier: cash conversion deteriorates materially despite sustained growth

unknowns.unknown: Exact data-center share of backlog is not disclosed in reviewed evidence.

claims.claim: Record sales, strong orders/backlog and cash growth support execution, but lower segment margin year over year despite growth is a real present-day caution on mix and integration economics.
The reviewed evidence does not establish a current financing/dilution or governance defect; those dimensions remain unasserted rather than manufactured as bearish evidence.

factors.name: thesisQuality
factors.basis: Demand transmission is physically grounded and supported by order/backlog evidence, with explicit margin/integration risk.

factors.name: pricingPower
factors.basis: Strong demand/backlog supports commercial position, but lower segment margin cautions against inferring unlimited pricing power.

risks.risk: Electrical demand or project timing can normalize after elevated backlog growth.
Acquisition integration and mix can dilute incremental returns; segment margin was lower year over year despite strong growth.
Headline data-center TAM should not be equated with Eaton-specific backlog or pricing because exact data-center backlog share is undisclosed here.

causalEdges.mechanism: growth can create less value if acquired or lower-margin mix dilutes profitability
causalEdges.falsifier: segment margins expand sustainably as acquired capacity and backlog convert

contradictions.claimA: Strong sales/order growth suggests operating leverage potential.
contradictions.claimB: Reported segment margin was lower year over year.
contradictions.disposition: material caution but not a blocker; monitor mix and integration as backlog converts.

unknowns.unknown: Exact data-center backlog exposure is not established.
No source-addressed current financing/dilution or governance defect is established in reviewed Beta inputs.
